extracted.intended_audience: law scholars, patent policymakers, IP litigators, and empirical researchers studying patent litigation
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical law-review study identifying and comparing the characteristics of patents litigated many times (most‑litigated, defined as 8+ suits between 2000–2007) to a control set litigated once, using the Stanford IP Litigation Clearinghouse and patent-level bibliometric and prosecution variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most-litigated patent threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is classified as 'most‑litigated' if it has been litigated eight or more times between 2000 and 2007 (including pending cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count separate lawsuits (declaratory-judgment actions included); multiple defendants in a single proceeding count as one suit for this measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control-set patent threshold (once-litigated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control patents are those litigated only once during the 2000–2007 period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as baseline to compare characteristics of most‑litigated patents; randomly selected sample of 106 such patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source: Stanford IP Litigation Clearinghouse (IPLC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the IPLC (lexmachina.stanford.edu) which collects every patent‑infringement suit filed since Jan. 1, 2000 in searchable format and links suits to the patents in suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPLC enables identification and verification of patents in suits; electronic filing coverage varies by district so manual collection may be needed for underinclusive districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention in which data processing is a sufficiently critical element that at least one claim element in the patent consists of data processing—the actual manipulation of data—regardless of whether the code carrying out that data processing is on a magnetic storage medium or embedded in a chip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes firmware; used as a broad category for regression and descriptive statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Pure software
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention consisting only of data processing; all claim elements in the patent consist of data processing (with trivial non‑data elements such as generic input/output/storage allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subset of software; excludes inventions with meaningful non‑data processing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Software business method
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset of software patents covering methods for conducting business transactions—narrowly defined here to claims that obviously cover automated generation of customer proposals, advertising, and the use of online catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a narrow definition to avoid overbroad inclusion of business-related software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Mechanical
rubrics_metrics.description: A process, machine, or product that consists solely of the use of mechanical parts, sometimes combined with heat, hydraulics, pneumatics, or other power sources; or an invention in which the above is a critical part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not a catchall 'other' category; may overlap with electronics or other technologies when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Electronics
rubrics_metrics.description: A process, machine, or product in which the invention or a critical part thereof makes use of traditional electronic circuitry or involves electric‑energy storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May overlap with chemistry, optics, or mechanics; treat as distinct when electronics is a critical part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Optics (other than imaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: A process, machine, or product in which the invention or a critical part thereof employs light waves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optics patents may also be classified in electronics or chemistry where relevant; excludes imaging (separate category).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Imaging
rubrics_metrics.description: A process, machine, or product in which the invention or a critical part thereof involves the creation or processing of images for various purposes (analog or digital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority have medical uses but include security, meteorology, and other imaging applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Biotechnology
rubrics_metrics.description: A process involving advanced genetic techniques intended to construct new microbial, plant, or animal strains; a product created from such a process; or the way such a process or product is used in biotechnology research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disaggregate by genetic technique; treat biotechnology broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology area: Chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: A process consisting of chemical reactions, a product resulting from such a process, an invention in which a chemical process or product is a critical part, or an invention consisting of a purportedly novel use of chemical substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes novel metal alloys and nonmetallic amalgams; may overlap with electronics or optics where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Computer
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry encompassing both software and computer‑hardware inventions, including hardware products and machines/processes for making computer hardware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semiconductor inventions are not automatically in computer industry even if they are computer components; classify based on intended industry use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Semiconductor
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions intended to advance the state of the art in researching, designing, or fabricating semiconductor chips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some patents may belong to both semiconductor and computer industry categories when the intended use overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Electronics (industry)
rubrics_metrics.description: A somewhat narrower industry-oriented version of the electronics technology category; includes patents involving electronics but excludes inventions better attributed to the industry for which the electronics is intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: packaging for integrated circuits is classified to the targeted computer/semiconductor industry rather than electrical industry where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Medical
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions used for research on, diagnosis, or treatment of diseases or other abnormal conditions in humans or animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes pharmaceutical drugs (separate industry category).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Pharmaceutical
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents on drugs for treating diseases or other abnormal conditions in humans or animals, and processes for producing or using such drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished from medical industry category; pharmacological inventions are here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Biotechnology (industry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry category corresponding to the biotechnology technology area, used when inventions are intended for biotechnology companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when the intended industry, not just the technique, is biotechnology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Chemical
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents dealing primarily with making, transporting, and using chemical substances (except pharmaceutical drugs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader than chemistry technology area because it includes inventions intended for use by chemical companies that may not employ chemical techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents intended to advance the state of the art in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both hardware and software inventions targeted at communications industry needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents on inventions related to vehicles of any type or the provision of transportation services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify inventions by intended industry application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Energy and utility services
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents associated with power generation, transport, consumption, or delivery of public utility services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inventions across generation, transmission, consumption, and utility service delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Financial
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes and products associated with providing financial services of various kinds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often software‑implemented and may also be classified in the computer industry category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Consumer goods and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents on products and services intended for personal consumer purposes, including methods for marketing, buying, or delivering personal consumer goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often software‑implemented and may overlap with computer industry category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry area: Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions related to the erection or maintenance of structures, or to excavation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify construction‑related inventions and processes here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity-status classification (12 classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify patent owners into one of twelve entity-status classes to distinguish practicing from various types of nonpracticing entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The twelve classes used: (1) Acquired patents; (2) University heritage or tie; (3) Failed startup; (4) Corporate heritage; (5) Individual-inventor-started company; (6) University/Government/NGO; (7) Startup, pre-product; (8) Product company; (9) Individual; (10) Undetermined; (11) Industry consortium; (12) IP subsidiary of product company. Class 8 denotes practicing/product companies; other classes typically denote nonpracticing entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Acquired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents owned by entities that acquired them (e.g., via purchase) rather than developing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often treated as nonpracticing when owner does not practice the patents themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: University heritage or tie
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents with university heritage or ties (originating from universities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be owned/licensed by universities or derived entities; consider small‑entity status implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Failed startup
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents originating from startups that failed commercially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often result in patents being enforced/licensed by nonpracticing owners after company failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Corporate heritage
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents that trace to established corporations (heritage ownership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be enforced by corporate owners or spun out to other entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Individual-inventor-started company
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents originating from companies started by individual inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be practicing or nonpracticing depending on company status and productization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: University/Government/NGO
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents owned by universities, government bodies, or non‑governmental organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May have different enforcement practices and incentives than commercial entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Startup, pre-product
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents from startups that have not yet produced a product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely to enforce via licensing or litigation rather than product sales; treated distinct from product companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Product company
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners that actually make products (practicing entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class 8 in the study; distinguished from nonpracticing entities for policy implications (e.g., injunctive relief and lost-profits entitlement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual patent owners enforcing their patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be small entities for fee/status purposes; enforcement patterns differ from corporate owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Undetermined
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners whose entity status could not be identified after diligent search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded from entity-status analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: Industry consortium
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents owned/controlled by a consortium of industry participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement patterns and incentives may differ from single‑owner entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity class: IP subsidiary of product company
rubrics_metrics.description: An intellectual‑property holding subsidiary of a product company that holds and enforces patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May or may not practice the patents directly; relevant to 'troll' debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the patent owner is an individual, university, or small business (small‑entity) as opposed to a large business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a categorical variable in regression analyses; small‑entity status affects maintenance fees and possibly enforcement incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment before litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether ownership of the patent had been assigned after issuance and before the first litigation of that patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a categorical predictor in logistic regression; assignment prior to litigation may signal transfers to nonpracticing owners or trolls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of U.S. nonprovisional applications in chain (continuations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of nonprovisional U.S. applications in the prosecution chain leading to the particular patent (measure of continuation practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a continuous predictor; most‑litigated patents average more continuations (e.g., mean 4.32) than once‑litigated patents; continuation usage is interpreted as evidence of strategic prosecution and possible indication of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family / number of continuations as value indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of continuations and family size as indicators of private patent value (litigated patents tend to have more continuations/family members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report means/medians and test significance; interpret high continuation counts as signals owners invest more prosecution resources in valuable patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total number of forward citations (raw)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of forward citations — later patents that cite the patent at issue as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an indicator of patent value but must be adjusted for age and changing citation patterns over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted number of forward citations (age‑cohort adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward citations adjusted by placing each patent into an issue‑year cohort and dividing its forward citations by the cohort average to account for patent age and temporal changes in citation rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustment method from Hall, Jaffe & Trajtenberg; necessary because older patents have had more time to accrue citations and citation norms change over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-citations (raw and adjusted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations to the patent in subsequent patents issued to the same inventor or assignee; counted both raw and adjusted for patent age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-citations are an independent indicator of private value (portfolio building); identify self-citations carefully given multiple inventors and ownership changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of the number of claims in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a predictor variable; more claims have been correlated in prior work with higher patent value and litigation likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward citations / prior art references
rubrics_metrics.description: References the patent makes to prior U.S. patents, foreign patents, and nonpatent prior art (other publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as variables in regressions and descriptive analysis; differences in backward citation counts between groups can be highly significant and informative about prosecution strategy and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of logistic regression for multivariate analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ logistic regression to test which patent characteristics remain significant predictors of being most‑litigated after accounting for interactions/correlations among variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two logistic regressions were run: one including patent characteristics + technology areas; another with patent characteristics + industry areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Report results only when confidence level is greater than 99% (p‑value < 0.01) unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accepted social‑science conventions but the study adopts a stringent 99% confidence threshold for reported findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling skewed distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply normalization techniques (e.g., log transformation) to skewed variables before making bivariate statistical comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward citations and similar bibliometric measures are highly skewed; use log transform to make differences clearer and appropriate for t‑tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort adjustment method for forward citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Place each patent into a one‑year cohort based on issue year, divide its forward citation count by the cohort average to get an adjusted citation measure, then average adjusted citations across the data set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method derived from Hall, Jaffe & Trajtenberg (NBER patent‑citations data file); improves comparability across patent ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting declaratory-judgment actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include declaratory-judgment actions in the count of suits (subject to pre‑2007 rules requiring reasonable apprehension of imminent suit; post‑MedImmune standard allows 'actual controversy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat DJ actions as suits for purposes of litigation‑frequency counts; be mindful of doctrinal changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting only separate lawsuits (not defendants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count only separate lawsuits—many patent lawsuits are filed against multiple defendants in a single proceeding and should be counted as a single suit for litigation-frequency metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents double‑counting when multiple defendants are included in one complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: litigation as signal of private patent value
rubrics_metrics.description: Litigation frequency is treated as an indicator of private value (value to owner), supported by prior empirical and economic literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors defend litigation‑value connection; caveat that litigation indicates private value but does not provide a quantitative measure of value in itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of nonpracticing entities vs. 'patent trolls'
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify patent owners as practicing (Class 8 product companies) vs. various nonpracticing entity classes; analyze the prevalence of nonpracticing entities among most‑litigated patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the definitional choices: calling an owner a 'troll' depends on the chosen definition (e.g., anyone who does not practice vs. companies enforcing patents they didn't develop). Report results for both practicing vs nonpracticing and for each entity class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple descriptive and bivariate comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform descriptive statistics and bivariate comparisons for technology and industry areas, adjusting variables where necessary and reporting tables of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some categories have small observation counts, some technology/industry areas are defined but excluded from statistical testing when sample sizes are too small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion rules for entity-status analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents with undetermined entity status (Class 10) are classified as 'Undetermined' and excluded from entity‑status analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure diligence in identification and exclude ambiguous cases from certain analyses to avoid misclassification bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution regarding industry/category overlaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology categories are not necessarily mutually exclusive; industry categories also overlap; modern inventions often involve multiple technologies and cross industry boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying, accept some non‑mutual exclusivity and note potential crossovers in analysis and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting conventions for statistical tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Report means, medians, standard deviations, p‑values (e.g., one sample t‑test with log transformation), and note significance (Yes/No) for comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use log transforms when skewed; include both raw and transformed/adjusted measures to make distributions and differences transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: industry concentration and cross‑licensing effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider industry structure effects (e.g., semiconductor industry concentration and cross‑licensing reduce litigation likelihood) when interpreting industry differences in litigation frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for industry‑specific institutional features that alter litigation incentives when drawing conclusions from comparative statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of patent outcome variables
rubrics_metrics.description: This Article does not address the outcomes of the lawsuits (e.g., verdicts, settlements); such outcomes are reserved for a companion paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between litigation frequency as a predictor/indicator and case outcomes which are separate analytical questions.
